videos.script: Your API answers anybody who asks, as fast as they ask. That is fine until one client asks a thousand times a second. {{flood}} Sometimes that client is an attacker. Far more often it is a bug. A loop nobody stopped, or a retry that never gives up. {{loop}} Either way, everybody else waits behind it. This lesson puts a limit in front of the books. Each client is known by its key, and each key gets its own allowance. {{keys}} You meet the counters that do the limiting. A fixed window, which is simple and has a hole at its edge. And a token bucket, which allows a burst and then a steady pace. {{bucket}} You send a burst at your own server and watch it answer 429, with a header saying when to come back. {{burst}} Then you write the other side. A client that waits, a little longer each time, instead of hammering. {{client}} And at the end, the question every real deployment asks. What happens to the count when there is more than one server? {{servers}}
